title: Setting Up Your Bedroom Temperature Sensor
section: Part 1 · Connect the base station to your internet
text:
Part 1 · Connect the base station to your internet

Video: Setting up the base station (coming soon)




1


Find your internet router
This is the box your internet provider gave you — the one that gives you Wi-Fi.
It is usually in the hallway, lounge room or study, near the phone socket. It often has one or more aerials and a row of small green lights.

You can see a row of small square sockets on the back.








2


Plug the cable into the router
Take the network cable from your pack. Plug one end into a spare socket on the back of your router.
The right sockets are labelled LAN and are often coloured yellow.
Do not use the socket labelled WAN or DSL. Leave any cables that are already plugged in exactly where they are.

Both ends click into place and do not pull out easily.










3


Plug the cables into the base station
The base station has two sockets on the back. Turn it round so you can see them.
Push the network cable into the wider socket on the right. It clicks when it is in.
Push the small end of the charging cable into the socket on the left. Leave the other end of it loose for now.

Both cables are pushed all the way in.










4


Turn the base station on
Plug the loose end of the charging cable into the power adapter, then plug the adapter into a wall socket.
Switch the socket on at the wall. On the front of the base station there is a row of small symbols. The exclamation mark on the left will light up red. This just means it has power — it has not found your internet yet.

The exclamation mark on the left is lit red.









5


Wait one minute
The red exclamation mark will go out and the cloud symbol next to it will light up green. Green means the base station has found your internet and is working.
Once the cloud is green, you are finished with Part 1. Leave the base station plugged in and switched on for the whole study.

The cloud symbol is lit green.












Important



Do not unplug the base station or switch the socket off overnight. If it is unplugged, we stop receiving your readings.

title: Setting Up Your Bedroom Temperature Sensor
section: Part 2 · Put the sensor on your bedroom wall
text:
Part 2 · Put the sensor on your bedroom wall


6


Choose the right spot
The sensor comes clipped into a white holder, and it is the holder that sticks to the wall. Pick a clear patch of wall in the room where you sleep, close to your bed.
Choose a spot that is out of direct sunlight, and away from windows, fans, heaters and air-conditioning vents.
Avoid putting it behind curtains, inside a wardrobe, or directly above a lamp. Anything warm or draughty nearby will give us the wrong reading.

The spot stays shaded all day and nothing blows air across it.








7


Peel off the paper backing
Turn the holder over — two long strips run all the way down the back, each covered with a paper backing.
Peel the paper off both strips. Try not to touch the sticky surfaces with your fingers — they hold better if you don’t.








8


Press it onto the wall
Press the two prongs with the sticky strips flat onto the wall, not the front of the holder, and hold for 30 seconds.
Then leave it alone for an hour before touching it again, so the adhesive can set. The sensor can stay clipped in the holder the whole time.

The holder stays put when you gently let go.









9


Pull out the plastic tab
The sensor arrives with a small plastic tab sticking out of it. This keeps the battery from running down before you start.
Take hold of the tab and pull it straight out. The sensor will beep once as it switches itself on.
Throw the tab away. You will not need it again.

You heard the sensor beep, and the tab is out.









10


Put the sensor into the holder
Hold the holder steady with one hand and slide the sensor down into it from the top.
The label goes at the top, facing you. Push it down until it sits flat in the holder.

The sensor sits in the holder and does not slide out.













NoteGood to know



The strips are paint-safe and will not mark your wall. If the holder does not stick, or comes away later, call us and we will send you new strips.
crumbs: Setting Up Your Bedroom Temperature Sensor

title: Setting Up Your Bedroom Temperature Sensor
text:
Part 3 · Changing the battery
You do not need to check the battery yourself. We can see how much charge is left from our end. If it starts running low we will post you a spare battery and let you know it needs changing. Nothing here is needed during set-up.

Video: Changing the sensor battery (coming soon)




11


Take the sensor out of its holder
Leave the white holder stuck on the wall — it stays there.
Hold the holder steady with one hand and slide the sensor straight up and out of it with the other.

The sensor is in your hand and the holder is still on the wall.








12


Open the sensor
You will need something thin and flat, such as a butter knife or a small flat screwdriver.
There is a small slot in the edge of the sensor, made for exactly this. Push the flat tip into the slot, then rotate the tool a quarter turn. Do not lever or lift it — the cover pops off as you turn.

The outer cover has come away.









13


Take off the second cover
Under the first cover is a second white cover. Take it off the same way — tip into the slot, then a quarter turn.

Both covers are off and the battery shows.








14


Swap the battery
The round silver battery sits in a socket, held in place by two small metal clips.
Do not try to prise it upwards. Rest the flat edge of your tool against the side of the battery and give it a gentle push sideways — it will slide smoothly out from under the clips.
Slide the new battery in the same way, the same way up, with the writing facing you, until it sits under both clips. You should hear a short beep.

The new battery sits flat under both clips and you heard a beep.








15


Close it and put it back
Line the two halves up and press them together all the way round until they click shut.
Slide the sensor back down into the holder on the wall. Nothing needs to be stuck back on.
You can throw the old battery away yourself — many supermarkets and hardware shops have a battery recycling bin. Until then, keep it well out of reach of children and pets.

The sensor is back in its holder on the wall.

title: Setting Up Your Bedroom Temperature Sensor
text:
If something doesn’t look right







If this happens
Try this




The exclamation mark is still red after 5 minutes
Check both ends of the network cable are pushed all the way in. Unplug the base station at the wall, wait 10 seconds, and plug it back in.


There is no spare socket on the back of my router
Please do not unplug anything. Call us and we will arrange an alternative.


No symbols light up at all
Check the wall socket is switched on, and try a different wall socket.


The holder has come off the wall
Keep the sensor and holder safe and call us. We will send you new sticky strips.


I did not hear a beep when I changed the battery
Take the battery out, turn it over, and check the flat side faces the same way as before. If there is still no beep, call us.









TipNeed a hand?



Please call us — we would much rather help than have you guess.

title: Setting Up Your Mattress Topper
text:
Note



Only set up the mattress topper after the research team has called to tell you it is time. It arrives separately from the rest of your equipment, closer to summer. These instructions are still being finalised, and the printed booklet in the topper’s box will be the final version.

title: Setting Up Your Mattress Topper
text:
Before you begin — items required
These items are in your pack. Check each one is there. If anything is missing, call us before you start.




Mattress topper





Control unit





Power cord





Remote control



You will also need a jug of water and a power point within reach of the bed.

title: Setting Up Your Mattress Topper
text:
Part 1 · Setting up the topper
Watch a short video of these steps:



1


Put the topper on the bed
Strip the bed down to the bare mattress. Lay the topper on top with the grey side facing up.
Put it close to one side edge of the mattress for now — you will slide it across to the middle at the end of Step 2.
Point the end with the tube towards the head or the foot of the bed, whichever is closer to a power point.

The topper lies flat, grey side up, with the tube end at the head or foot.









2


Secure the elastic straps
The topper has two long elastic straps.
At the head of the bed, tuck both straps down between the mattress and its base. Run them along underneath the mattress and bring them out at the foot of the bed.
Now slide the topper across so it sits in the middle of the mattress. This pulls the straps snug.

The straps run under the mattress and the topper sits in the middle without sliding.








3


Connect the tube to the control unit
Stand the control unit on the floor beside the bed, at the end you chose in Step 1.
Push the connector tube firmly into the socket on the control unit until it stops.
Make sure the tube runs freely and is not kinked, pinched under a bed leg, or across a walkway.

The tube is fully seated and does not pull out with a gentle tug.








4


Plug in and switch on
Plug the power cord into the control unit, then into the wall socket, and switch the socket on.
Turn the control unit on to standby.

The control unit display lights up.








5


Fill with water
Take the cap off the water tank on the top of the control unit and pour water in until it is close to the top, leaving a small gap below the opening.
The topper will draw water in, so the level will drop. Wait a moment, then top it back up. Repeat until the level stops falling.
Screw the cap back on firmly.

The water level holds steady close to the top and the cap is back on.








6


Set the temperature
Use the two arrow buttons on the top of the control unit to set the temperature. The up arrow makes the bed warmer, the down arrow makes it cooler.
Then make the bed as usual, with your sheet over the topper.

The display shows the temperature you set.












Important



Do not fold, sit on, or place heavy objects on the topper, and keep the tube clear of bed legs and castors. Fluid runs through it, and a kink or crush stops the topper working.

title: Setting Up Your Mattress Topper
text:
Part 2 · Topping up the water
The topper uses a little water over time, so the level in the tank slowly drops. The control unit tells you when it needs topping up.
Watch how it is done (the top-up is at 26 seconds):



7


Check the water level
You do not need to keep an eye on this. The control unit will let you know when the water is getting low — it beeps and shows a warning on the display.
When that happens, take the cap off the tank and look inside to see how far the water has dropped.

You can see how far down the water sits.








8


Top it up
Pour water in until it is close to the top again, leaving a small gap below the opening. The warning will clear once there is enough water.
Screw the cap back on firmly. You do not need to turn the unit off to do this.

The water is back up close to the top and the cap is back on.












TipWhile the study is running



Sleep on the topper every night, and leave the control unit plugged in and switched on for the whole study.
The topper is there to cool you, much like an air conditioner would. Set it to a level that keeps you cool, and adjust it whenever you like.

title: Setting Up Your Mattress Topper
text:
If something doesn’t look right







If this happens
Try this




The topper does not feel cool
Check the water is close to the top of the tank, and check the tube is not kinked or trapped under a bed leg.


The control unit is beeping or showing a warning
Top the water up close to the top of the tank. If the warning stays on, call us.


There is water on the floor or the bed feels damp
Switch the wall socket off, put a towel down, and call us straight away. Do not keep using it.


The topper has slid out of place
Pull the bed away from the wall, re-hook the elastic straps at each corner, and pull them snug.


The control unit is noisy
A soft hum is normal. If it rattles, gurgles loudly, or keeps you awake, call us.









TipNeed a hand?



Please call us — we would much rather help than have you guess.

title: Setting Up Your Fitbit
section: Part 1 · Set up the app and connect your Fitbit
text:
Part 1 · Set up the app and connect your Fitbit


1


Download the Google Health app
On your phone, open the App Store (iPhone) or the Play Store (Android).
Search for Google Health and download it. It is free. The app used to be called Fitbit, so do not worry if you were expecting that name.

The app appears on your phone screen with a heart-shaped icon.








2


Charge and turn on the Fitbit
Put the Fitbit on its charger for a few minutes before you start.
If you are not sure how to put it on the charger, Part 3 of this guide (steps 12 and 13) shows you how.
To turn it on, squeeze both sides of the tracker at once, or tap the screen firmly twice.

The screen lights up.








3


Sign in to the app
Open the app and sign in with a Google account. You can use one you already have, or make a new one.
Use the same account for the whole study. The account you sign in with is what sends your readings to us. Keep a note of which one you used — we will ask you for it in Step 8.

You are signed in and the app opens on its main screen.








4


Tap the device icon
In the app, tap the device icon to open the Connections screen.
Under Devices, tap where it offers to connect a Fitbit tracker.

You can see the words Add connections on the screen.








5


Choose your device
Choose Inspire 3 from the list of devices. Allow Bluetooth when the app asks. On an Android phone, also allow location and nearby devices.

The app starts looking for your tracker.








6


Enter the code from the Fitbit
Leave the Fitbit on its charger and close to your phone while the app looks for it. When a four-digit code appears on the Fitbit screen, type it into the app.
The app may then install an update. This can take a few minutes — keep the Fitbit beside your phone until it finishes.

The app accepts the code and moves on.








7


Answer the questions
The app will ask for your height, weight and sex. It uses these to work out distance and calories.
It may also offer to set up goals, notifications and a Premium trial. Fill these in or skip them as you like.

The app shows your Fitbit as connected.








8


Email us straight away
Your readings will not reach us until you do this.
Send us an email with the address of the Google account you signed in with. Please do this as soon as the app says your Fitbit is connected, not later.

Tap to show the email address


If you have any further questions about setting up the Fitbit, please contact Dr Fergus O’Connor:

Tap to show the phone number



You have sent us the email.












Important



Keep the app installed and stay signed in for the whole study. If you sign out or delete the app, we stop receiving your readings.

title: Setting Up Your Fitbit
text:
Part 2 · Changing the band
Only do this if the band that came fitted is too tight. Otherwise skip to Part 3.
Watch how it is done:



9


Press the small pin in
Turn the tracker over so you are looking at the back. The band joins the tracker at the top and at the bottom.
At the end of the band nearest the top, there is a small pin set into the band. Press it in with your thumbnail — push it sideways, in towards the centre of the band — and hold it there.







10


Lift that end of the band away
While you hold the pin in, tilt that end of the band away from the tracker and it will come free.
Do the same at the other end.

The band comes free of the tracker.








11


Fit the new band
Line the new band up with the end of the tracker, press its pin in towards the centre of the band, slide it into place, and let the pin go.
Give the band a gentle tug to check it is holding.

You hear or feel a small click, and the band does not pull off.

title: Setting Up Your Fitbit
text:
Part 3 · Charging the Fitbit
Charge the Fitbit every few days, or whenever the app tells you it is low or you notice the battery is getting low. Charging takes about an hour.
Charge it during the day rather than overnight, so it is on your wrist while you sleep. A good time is while you are in the shower, or while you are sitting down reading or working — put it on the charger, then straight back on your wrist afterwards.
Watch how it is done:



12


Line up the gold contacts
Turn the tracker over. Across the top of the back there is a row of small gold dots.
Inside the charger there are matching gold pins. Hold the tracker so the two sets of contacts face each other.

The gold contacts on the tracker are facing the gold pins in the charger.








13


Clip the tracker into the charger
Press the tracker down into the charger until the small tabs at each end grip it. It should feel firmly held and not fall out if you turn it over.
Plug the other end of the cable into the small power adapter from your pack, then plug the adapter into a wall socket and switch it on.

A battery symbol appears on the tracker screen.

title: Setting Up Your Fitbit
text:
If something doesn’t look right







If this happens
Try this




The screen will not turn on
Put it on the charger for 10 minutes, then squeeze both sides or tap the screen firmly twice.


I cannot find Google Health in the store
Search for the exact words Google Health. The publisher is listed as Google. Do not download an app called Fitbit.


I am not sure which account I used
Open the app and tap your profile to see the email you are signed in with. Tell us if it has changed.


The band feels too tight or leaves a mark
Loosen it by one hole. If it is still tight, fit the larger band using Part 2.


The app says my Fitbit is not connected
Keep your phone near the tracker, check Bluetooth is switched on, then open the app and wait a minute.









TipNeed a hand?



Please call us — we would much rather help than have you guess.

title: Need a hand?
text:
About the study
Can a mattress topper preserve nocturnal autonomic function in older adults during summer? A randomised crossover trial is being conducted by Griffith University and has been approved by the Griffith University Human Research Ethics Committee (GU Ref No: HREC/2026/0662).
If you have any concerns or complaints about the ethical conduct of the research project, you can contact the Senior Manager, Research Ethics Integrity and Governance on (07) 3735 4375 or research-ethics@griffith.edu.au.






WarningIf you feel unwell



The Fitbit is a consumer wellness device, not a medical device, and its readings are not a diagnosis. If a notification concerns you, or you feel unwell at any time during the study, please see your GP, or call 000 in an emergency.

section: A few things that matter for the whole study
text:
A few things that matter for the whole study

Keep the Google Health app installed and stay signed in with the same Google account for the whole study, and email us that account’s address as soon as your Fitbit is connected. If you sign out or the account changes, we stop receiving your readings.
Leave the base station plugged in and switched on, day and night.
Charge the Fitbit during the day, not overnight, so it is on your wrist while you sleep.

Temperature wall sensor

Fitbit Inspire 3

title: Returning Your Study Equipment
text:
Part 1 · Getting the equipment ready
Watch how the sticky strips come off the wall:



1


Take the sensor and holder off the wall
Hold the white holder steady and slide the sensor straight up and out of it.
Underneath the holder there are two small pull tabs. Pull each one slowly straight down the wall — down, not out towards you. The strip will stretch and then let go, and the holder will come away cleanly.
Take it slowly and let the strip stretch — that is what releases it. Keep pulling downwards the whole way, rather than away from the wall.

The sensor, the holder and both strips are off the wall.










2


Unplug the base station and all of its cables
Switch the wall socket off first, then unplug the power adapter from the wall.
Unplug the network cable from the back of your router and from the base station. Then unplug the base station’s charging cable from the power adapter.
Four things go back: the base station, the network cable, the charging cable and the power adapter. Leave any of your own cables exactly where they are.

You have all four pieces together, and your router is left with only its own cables.








3


Take the sensor out of the water tank
The small water tank temperature sensor was already fitted when the pod arrived. It sits in the filling area of the water tank.
Lift it out and set it aside. Nothing needs to be unplugged or switched off.
Check the silvery temperature sensor is still attached. If it is not, tip the water out of the tank, turn the unit over and let the sensor fall out. Pat it dry before it goes in the bag.

The sensor is out of the water tank and undamaged.










4


Take off the Fitbit and gather the rest
Take the Fitbit off your wrist.
Open the Google Health app on your phone one last time, with the tracker still beside you, and leave it open for a minute. This lets your last few days of readings reach us.
Then sign out of your Google account in the app. Once you are signed out you can delete the app from your phone if you like.
Four things go back: the Fitbit tracker, its charging cable, its power adapter and the band extender.

You are signed out of the app and all four pieces are together in one place.

title: Returning Your Study Equipment
text:
Part 2 · Posting it back
A sealable postage bag came with the equipment we sent you. The return address is already printed on it, so there is nothing to write and nothing to pay.


5


Put everything in the bag
Put all the items from the list into the postage bag.

Everything on the list is inside the bag.








6


Seal the bag
Peel the strip off the sticky edge of the bag, fold the flap over, and press it down firmly along its whole length.
Check the return address label is still stuck on and easy to read. Do not write anything else on the bag.

The bag is sealed shut and the address label is clearly visible.








7


Take it to any post office
Hand the bag over at the counter of any Australia Post office. Postage is already paid, so there is nothing to buy.
Please post it within one to two weeks of the study finishing. We will contact you at the end of the study to arrange all of this with you and make sure everything has gone smoothly.

The bag has been handed over at the counter.

title: Returning Your Study Equipment
text:
If something doesn’t look right







If this happens
Try this




I cannot find the postage bag
Call us and we will post you another one. Please do not pay for your own postage.


Something is missing or broken
Post the rest of the equipment anyway and let us know what is missing.


A strip snapped before it released
Take hold of what is left of the tab and keep pulling slowly straight down the wall. If there is no tab left to grip, slide dental floss down behind the holder to cut the strip away from the wall.


I cannot get to a post office
Call us — we can arrange another way for you to get the equipment back to us.
